check_service_status.description: Check whether chucknorris.io is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being throttled at the edge is reported separately from being down.
check_service_status.name: check_service_status

get_joke_by_id.description: Get one specific fact by its id, for re-posting a fact an earlier step found. Ids are opaque strings the service assigns once and never reuses, so an id stored last month still means the same fact. A full chucknorris.io joke URL is accepted in place of the bare id.

joke.text: Chuck Norris can divide by zero.
joke.value: Chuck Norris can divide by zero.

get_joke_by_id.name: get_joke_by_id

parameters.description: The fact's id, or the full chucknorris.io link to it. Usually this comes from an earlier step: every action here returns the id of each fact it hands back.
parameters.name: joke_id

parameters.description: Swap someone else's name in for Chuck Norris, the way the service's own Slack app does. 'Ada' turns 'Chuck Norris can divide by zero' into 'Ada can divide by zero'. The untouched fact is always returned too, as 'value', so you can see whether the swap landed: a fact that never names him in full comes back unchanged. Leave empty to post it as written.
parameters.name: name

get_joke_of_the_day.description: Pick one fact for a day and keep picking that same fact all day. A random draw gives a different one on every call, so a daily workflow that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, posts two different facts for the one day. This one is fixed by the date: the same date always gives the same fact, and tomorrow gives a different one. Add a seed of your own to have two workspaces post different facts on the same day.
get_joke_of_the_day.display_name: Get the joke of the day
get_joke_of_the_day.display_str_template: Get the Chuck Norris joke of the day for {0}.

joke.text: Chuck Norris counted to infinity. Twice.
joke.value: Chuck Norris counted to infinity. Twice.

get_joke_of_the_day.name: get_joke_of_the_day

parameters.description: The day to pick a fact for. Leave empty for today in UTC, which is what a scheduled step wants.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: Only draw from this category. The service publishes categories such as animal, career, celebrity, dev, food, history, money, movie, music, science, sport and travel; run Get joke categories for the current list. Leave empty to draw from every fact, which is where most of them are: the catalogue is mostly uncategorised.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: Swap someone else's name in for Chuck Norris, the way the service's own Slack app does. 'Ada' turns 'Chuck Norris can divide by zero' into 'Ada can divide by zero'. The untouched fact is always returned too, as 'value', so you can see whether the swap landed: a fact that never names him in full comes back unchanged. Leave empty to post it as written.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Any text you like, mixed into the day so that two workspaces running this on the same day get different facts. Leave empty to share the day's fact with everyone else.
parameters.name: seed

parameters.description: Allow facts from the explicit category, which holds adult material. Off by default, so a step posting to a team channel cannot draw one by accident. Choosing the explicit category counts as asking for them, and is not filtered.
parameters.name: include_explicit

get_random_joke.description: Get one random Chuck Norris fact, ready to post, with a link back to it. Narrow it to a category such as dev or movie, or leave the category empty to draw from the whole catalogue. Swap in a colleague's name to personalise it. Explicit facts are skipped unless you ask for them.

get_random_jokes.description: Get several different Chuck Norris facts at once, up to 20, optionally all from one category. No fact is drawn twice in the same batch. The service returns one random fact per request, so a batch costs a request per fact and a little more; asking a small category for more than it holds returns what there is rather than failing.

get_random_jokes.name: get_random_jokes

parameters.description: How many facts to draw, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 5.
parameters.name: count

list_categories.description: List the categories a fact can be filtered by, each flagged for whether it is the adult one, so a step that builds a filter from this list can leave that one out without knowing its name in advance.
list_categories.display_str_template: Get the Chuck Norris joke categories.
list_categories.name: list_categories

search_jokes.description: Find the facts that mention something, a name, a language or a place, best match first. The service publishes no relevance of its own, so matches are ranked here with a whole-word hit worth far more than one buried inside a longer word. Narrow to a category, and see how many explicit matches were left out. The query must be 3 to 120 characters, which is the service's own limit.

matches.text: Chuck Norris can divide by zero.
matches.value: Chuck Norris can divide by zero.

search_jokes.name: search_jokes

parameters.description: The word or phrase to look for in the facts, 3 to 120 characters.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only keep matches in this category. The service's search takes no category of its own, so this is applied to its results. Leave empty to search every fact.
parameters.name: category

parameters.description: How many matches to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 10. The total number of matches is always reported, however many are returned.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Allow facts from the explicit category, which holds adult material. Off by default, so a step posting to a team channel cannot draw one by accident. Choosing the explicit category counts as asking for them, and is not filtered.
parameters.name: include_explicit

description: Pull Chuck Norris facts from chucknorris.io, the free hand-curated joke API. Draw one at random or a batch of them, narrow to a category such as dev, movie or sport, search every fact for a subject, look one up by id, or pick a fact of the day that stays the same all day so a scheduled post never tells two. Swap a colleague's name in for Chuck Norris, and keep the explicit category out of a team channel: it is left out unless you ask for it.
